content:
Honestly, my DIY iPhone lens mod looks pretty ridiculous—but it actually makes the iPhone's camera more practical and a lot more fun to use.

What started as a solution to a one-off shooting problem has somehow become a tool I instinctively reach for…

One of the most enduring debates in the compact camera world is whether you actually need a viewfinder. Traditional camera enthusiasts used to argue endlessly about electronic viewfinders (EVF) versus optical ones, but EVFs have gotten so good that almost no one cares anymore.

Whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers real practical advantages over composing with the rear screen—especially in harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, it's hard to see the image clearly under intense sun, and the screen reflects easily.

In London this hasn't traditionally been a huge issue, but this summer we experienced record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

For me, though, the issue goes beyond that. I've noticed a difference in visual engagement between using a viewfinder and using the rear screen—with a viewfinder you see only the frame itself, but with the rear screen you take in the surrounding environment too. Sometimes it's precisely that sense of immersion that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camera for video recording a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was hands down the most compelling option, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end I decided it wasn't a dealbreaker, because I mostly use it indoors, and even when I go outside, attaching a large monitor with a sun hood solves most of the problems.

But sometimes I want something simpler to operate than a full rig with an extra monitor, so I found a simple accessory that's perfect for outdoor use. It's essentially a combination of a sun hood and a magnifying lens that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, giving you an experience similar to an optical viewfinder.

Recently I had a shoot that required using both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I went on location to do a quick test, and that viewfinder accessory was a big help. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone have similar-sized screens, I wondered whether the same accessory might also work on my iPhone.

The iPhone of course doesn't have a magnetic array, but the phone is light enough that simply holding it against the magnifier works perfectly. The result surprised me—especially being able to use the camera control button as a shutter.

Since then I've been using this accessory to shoot in all kinds of situations, and being able to see the screen clearly in intense sunlight, combined with that sense of immersion, has made the whole process far more enjoyable. My iPhone has long been my main camera, and with this DIY mod I've found myself just grabbing the phone in even more situations.

Genius or insanity? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments. If you're in the pro camp, I'm afraid I have to tell you that the model I bought appears to have been discontinued, and I've never seen a similar design made for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, be sure to drop a link in the comments.
